title: "Using CSS & SCSS with Quarto"
subtitle: "How I customized this website"
toc: true
---

Quarto websites use Bootstrap as a starting point. I used **SCSS** for site-wide choices such as colors and fonts, and **CSS** for specific page elements such as the home-page layout and skill cards.

## SCSS: site-wide styling

In `_quarto.yml`, I combined the built-in `flatly` theme with my own `theme.scss` file:

```yaml
format:
  html:
    theme: [flatly, theme.scss]
    css: styles.css
```

The SCSS variables change the design across the whole website:

```scss
/*-- scss:defaults --*/
$primary: #0b6e75;
$body-bg: #f6f4ef;
$body-color: #243443;
$headings-color: #102a43;
$navbar-bg: #102a43;
```

Changing one variable can update buttons, links, headings, and other Bootstrap components at the same time.

## CSS: component styling

I used regular CSS when I wanted to style one type of element. The two cards below use the same reusable class.

::: {.demo-grid}
::: {.demo-card .demo-card--teal}
### Consistent design

Shared spacing, borders, and typography make the cards feel related.
:::

::: {.demo-card .demo-card--amber}
### Responsive layout

The cards sit side by side on a larger screen and stack on a phone.
:::
:::

```css
.demo-grid {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(2, 1fr);
  gap: 1rem;
}

.demo-card {
  padding: 1.25rem;
  background: white;
  border-radius: 0.75rem;
}
```

## What I learned

- Use SCSS for repeated design decisions across the website.
- Use CSS for custom layouts and individual components.
- Test the site on different screen sizes.
- Keep text readable and provide alternative text for images.

[Quarto HTML theming documentation](https://quarto.org/docs/output-formats/html-themes.html)
